label: 23 August 1939
title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
summary: Germany and the Soviet Union promised nonaggression while secretly assigning spheres of influence across eastern Europe. Diplomatic records reveal the choices, deadlines, and territorial concessions behind a bargain that facilitated Germany’s attack on Poland.

label: 1 September 1939
title: Germany invades Poland
summary: German operational superiority met Polish resistance at bridges, fortified positions and railway crossings. The opening campaign depended on how quickly formations could move, recover and respond as threats developed along several axes.

label: 17 September 1939
title: The Soviet Union invades eastern Poland
summary: Moscow presented a prepared offensive as protection for threatened populations. Polish soldiers and civilians confronted shrinking opportunities for resistance, regrouping and escape as Soviet formations advanced from the east.

label: 28 September 1939
title: German–Soviet Boundary and Friendship Treaty
summary: The September treaty joined a revised territorial division to agreements on political suppression, selected migration, trade, and transit. Its implementation reached prisoners and refugees while Polish diplomacy and continued Allied war challenged the claim that Poland’s future was settled.

label: 26 October 1939
title: German occupation administration takes shape
summary: Annexation and the General Government gave German conquest different administrative forms. Decrees concerning property, labour, policing and local authority brought the occupiers’ power into daily life while the recognized Polish government continued abroad.
dateRationale: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum identifies 26 October as the date of German annexations and establishment of the General Government civilian administration.
